Spain.tactical_note: De la Fuente's Spain operates in a fluid 4-2-3-1 with high press and positional play inherited from Spain's tiki-taka tradition. Rodri anchors as a single CDM; Pedri and Dani Olmo rotate between CM and CAM roles. Width is generated by Nico Williams (LW) and Lamine Yamal (RW), both of whom dribble inside to create overloads. Oyarzabal plays as a false 9 / target striker. Main concern is Yamal's hamstring recovery — De la Fuente has said he may be limited in the opener vs Cape Verde.
Spain.fantasy_note: Pedri and Rodri are bankers in midfield. Oyarzabal is the safest FWD pick. Yamal carries a starting risk for MD1 but is nearly certain from MD2 onward — hold if you can. Nico Williams also carries an injury flag for MD1.

players.name: Lamine Yamal
players.doubt_reason: Hamstring injury April 2026; Barcelona advise max 15 mins in opener vs Cape Verde; coach says available but cautious

players.name: Nico Williams
players.doubt_reason: Injury suffered May 10 vs Valencia; did not play Spain warm-up vs Iraq; De la Fuente expects him ready for June 15 opener

review.reviewer_note: Full 26-man squad confirmed from ESPN and Sports Mole (announced May 25). Predicted XI aligns across multiple independent sources (Sports Mole, beIN Sports, PrizePicks, Bleacher Report). Injury status on Yamal and Williams sourced from ESPN and beIN Sports coach quotes dated June 4-5 2026.
key_uncertainties: Lamine Yamal may start on bench vs Cape Verde and play limited minutes — Yeremy Pino could start in his place
Nico Williams fitness unconfirmed for MD1; Alex Baena or Ferran Torres could deputize at LW
Cubarsi vs Eric Garcia at CB — Cubarsi is stronger prediction but Eric Garcia provides cover

Cape Verde.tactical_note: Bubista deploys a compact 4-2-3-1 built on two defensive blocks, sitting deep and transitioning quickly. Jamiro Monteiro and Kevin Pina operate as the double pivot, protecting a back four anchored by Logan Costa and Roberto Lopes. Ryan Mendes leads the attack at 36, using experience to link play. Dailon Livramento is the dynamic threat behind him. Cape Verde will look to frustrate Spain with low blocks and hit on the counter — their AFCON 2023 quarter-final run showed this works against quality opposition.
Cape Verde.fantasy_note: Ryan Mendes is the captain and focal point but at 36 his FPL ceiling is capped. Dailon Livramento is the best fantasy pick if you're selecting from Cape Verde — four goals in qualifying. Logan Costa is the defensive anchor. Team is a long shot to progress so value is limited overall.

review.reviewer_note: Full 26-man squad confirmed from The Football Faithful (June 4 2026), corroborated by FIFA.com announcement and ESPN squad lists. Bubista's preferred 4-2-3-1 system confirmed by multiple sources including RotoWire and LeagueLane. Specific slot allocations for wide players (Willy Semedo, Jovane Cabral) and exact right-back carry moderate uncertainty — squad has overlapping versatility in those positions. Pre-tournament friendly vs Serbia lineup (Lisbon, May 31) partially confirms Vozinha GK, Roberto Lopes, Logan Costa, Edilson Borges, Steven Moreira in defense from photo caption.
key_uncertainties: Right-back could be Kelvin Pires or João Paulo Fernandes rather than Steven Moreira — Moreira is right-back but has been used at other positions
Exact wide forward assignments between Nuno da Costa, Garry Rodrigues, Willy Semedo and Jovane Cabral are uncertain
Márquio Rosa listed as second GK but Vozinha (39) is confirmed starter and vice-captain

Saudi Arabia.tactical_note: Greek coach Donis was appointed only on April 23, replacing Hervé Renard just weeks before the tournament, leaving limited time to embed a new system. The squad defaults to a familiar 4-2-3-1 seen under Renard, with Kanno and Khaibari as the double pivot. Salem Al Dawsari operates centrally as the #10 with the most caps (108). Abdulhamid provides attacking width from right-back (he plays for Lens in France — the squad's only Europe-based outfield player). Al Buraikan leads the line. The late coaching change introduces genuine tactical uncertainty.
Saudi Arabia.fantasy_note: Salem Al Dawsari is the standout fantasy asset — captain, most creative player, highest caps. Al Buraikan is the goals threat with 15 international goals. Abdulhamid is an attacking RB worth monitoring for bonus points. Squad is almost entirely Saudi Pro League-based, limiting external data on form.

players.name: Nawaf Al Aqidi
players.doubt_reason: GK spot contested with veteran Al Owais; Al Aqidi identified as undisputed #1 by Olympics.com/Heavy but Al Owais has more World Cup experience (2022 hero vs Argentina)

review.reviewer_note: Full 26-man squad confirmed from Heavy.com (June 1 2026) and corroborated by Olympics.com and Yahoo Sports. 4-2-3-1 formation confirmed across MyLineups, Goal.com probable lineups and Fox Sports preview. Primary uncertainty is GK selection (Al Aqidi vs Al Owais) and the late coaching change (Donis appointed April 23) creating genuine tactical unpredictability. MyLineups shows Al Owais as starter; Heavy.com explicitly names Al Aqidi as 'undisputed number one'. Marked PROBABLE accordingly.
key_uncertainties: GK: Nawaf Al Aqidi vs Mohammed Al Owais — genuine competition, split opinions across sources
Georgios Donis appointed only 7 weeks before MD1 — his preferred tactical system is unknown and may differ from Renard-era 4-2-3-1
Left-back: Nawaf Boushal vs Sultan Al-Ghannam vs Moteb Al Harbi all compete for the slot
Nasser Al Dawsari vs Ziyad Al Johani for the left attacking midfield role

Uruguay.tactical_note: Bielsa's Uruguay deploys a high-energy 4-4-1-1 (sometimes described as a 4-3-3 depending on shape in possession) with exceptional midfield intensity. Valverde, Bentancur and Ugarte form a powerhouse three-man engine room covering every blade of grass. De Arrascaeta operates as the #10 linking midfield to Darwin Nunez. Muslera returns from international retirement for his fifth World Cup — a historic appearance record. The back four of Varela, Gimenez, Araujo and Olivera is among the strongest in South American football. Luis Suarez notably absent — not selected.
Uruguay.fantasy_note: Darwin Nunez is the standout FWD pick — in form at Al Hilal and Uruguay's primary goal threat. Federico Valverde is arguably the tournament's best midfielder value. De Arrascaeta is creative and consistent. Muslera is a sentimental pick at GK but not recommended over other options. Ronald Araujo is the defensive captain and CS pick.

review.reviewer_note: Full 26-man squad confirmed from beIN Sports (May 31 2026) and FIFA.com. Bielsa's preferred XI confirmed across MyLineups (4-4-1-1 with Muslera, Varela, Gimenez, Araujo, Olivera, Valverde, Bentancur, Ugarte, Maximiliano Araujo, De Arrascaeta, Nunez), FourFourTwo, and RotoWire Group H preview. Muslera return from retirement confirmed. Luis Suarez exclusion confirmed. The right midfield slot (Maximiliano Araujo vs Pellistri vs Brian Rodriguez) carries moderate uncertainty.
key_uncertainties: Right midfield/wing: Maximiliano Araujo vs Facundo Pellistri vs Brian Rodriguez — Bielsa may rotate
Formation interpretation varies by source (4-4-1-1 vs 4-3-3) — practical difference is minimal in Bielsa's pressing system
Muslera vs Rochet: Muslera was confirmed as starter despite coming out of international retirement — Rochet had been the regular #1 before Muslera's return

France.tactical_note: Deschamps' settled 4-2-3-1 features a Tchouameni-Rabiot double pivot to protect the back four and give the attacking three freedom to rotate. Mbappe leads the line as a false-nine who can drift wide. Olise and Dembele provide width and delivery; Doue operates as the creative link behind Mbappe. Kounde and Theo Hernandez provide aggressive fullback width. Maignan sweeps aggressively. France are Group I's dominant side by individual quality.
France.fantasy_note: Mbappe (ST) is the primary captaincy pick — set-piece taker, penalty taker, high-ceiling. Olise offers assist upside from RW. Dembele logs assists as a consistent wide creator. Doue is a differential with high involvement. Hernandez (LB) pushes far forward and contributes to attacks.

players.name: Desire Doue
players.doubt_reason: Competition from Bradley Barcola and Rayan Cherki for the left-of-10 role; Doue has the edge on current form

review.reviewer_note: All 11 starters and 4 bench drawn from the confirmed 26-man squad (FourFourTwo, June 3 2026). Lineup matches RotoWire Group I tactical preview (4-2-3-1). Camavinga, Kolo Muani, Ekitike correctly excluded as confirmed non-selections. Robin Risser and Malo Gusto omitted from bench as tactical rotation lower priority for MD1.
key_uncertainties: Doue vs Barcola vs Cherki for the third attacking midfield slot — all in squad, Doue marginally favoured by current form and age
Rabiot vs Manu Kone for the second pivot role — Rabiot has seniority and experience edge
Mbappe has a recent injury history flag but was training fully with squad pre-tournament

Senegal.tactical_note: Thiaw's settled 4-3-3 presses high and uses Mane as captain and creative fulcrum who drops into deeper pockets to link play. Koulibaly marshals the back four with authority. Double-Gueye pivot (Idrissa and Pape) provides defensive insurance and physicality. Diarra connects midfield to attack. Jackson leads the line with direct running and hold-up play. Ndiaye and Mane offer pace and guile on the flanks to exploit space on transition.
Senegal.fantasy_note: Mane is the senior set-piece taker and penalty option — leadership premium despite age. Nicolas Jackson (transferred from Chelsea to Bayern Munich) is the high-energy goal threat in the ST slot. Iliman Ndiaye provides assist and goal upside from RW. Krepin Diatta contributes from corners on the right flank.

players.name: Pape Gueye
players.doubt_reason: Lamine Camara and Pathe Ciss also in squad; Pape Gueye preferred by RotoWire for MD1 based on AFCON XI history

review.reviewer_note: All 11 starters and 4 bench drawn from confirmed 26-man squad (Soccergraph / Africa Top Sports, June 1-2 2026). Nicolas Jackson listed at Bayern Munich in squad source — confirmed transfer from Chelsea.
key_uncertainties: Pape Gueye vs Lamine Camara for the third midfield slot — both in squad, Pape Gueye has AFCON XI edge
Mane's age (34) creates minutes management concern; may be rotated against Iraq (MD3) but almost certain to start vs France (MD1)
AFCON title controversy (CAS appeal ongoing) as squad morale variable — coach Thiaw available for WC per source confirmation

Iraq.tactical_note: Arnold's Iraq are built on a compact 4-4-2 defensive block with quick transitions. Two banks of four stay narrow and deny central space. Iqbal and Al-Ammari form the central midfield pairing, with Iqbal providing creative vision and Al-Ammari providing the defensive shield and set-piece delivery. Amyn and Bayesh provide width on the flanks. Hussein and Al-Hamadi partner up top — Hussein the physical hold-up man, Al-Hamadi the mobile finisher who exploits space in behind on the counter. Set pieces are a primary attacking weapon.
Iraq.fantasy_note: Aymen Hussein is Iraq's primary set-piece and penalty option — high-volume involvement but low ceiling against top sides. Ali Al-Hamadi has the highest goal probability given pace and counter-attacking role. Zidane Iqbal is the creative outlet but low expected attacking returns. Iraq players carry low fantasy ceiling given the defensive game plan.

Whether Al-Hamadi starts vs a physical Norway side or is used from bench as impact substitute

Norway.tactical_note: Solbakken's 4-3-3 is built to maximise Haaland through direct vertical passes and fast transitions. Berge and Berg form a double pivot shielding the back four, with Odegaard as the advanced 8/10 operating in pockets between lines to feed Haaland. Sorloth and Nusa provide width from left and right, with Sorloth offering the physical striker backup and Nusa adding directness on the flank. The back four of Ryerson, Ajer, Ostigard and Wolfe provides Premier League-experienced depth. Nyland is the established first-choice GK. Norway press aggressively high and transition at speed.
Norway.fantasy_note: Haaland is the tournament's most dangerous striker and Norway's primary penalty taker — elite ceiling in all formats. Odegaard (if fit) is the assist engine; his fitness is the group's biggest narrative uncertainty. Nusa offers differential upside as a direct winger with 1v1 ability. Sorloth provides a secondary goal threat with 26 international goals to his name.

If Odegaard is unfit, Thorstvedt or Oscar Bobb likely steps in at CAM.

Whether Sorloth plays left wing or is part of a dual-striker system with Haaland (4-4-2 alternative) if Odegaard is unavailable

Argentina.tactical_note: Scaloni's near-certain default. E.Martinez anchors; Molina and Tagliafico push high as attacking fullbacks. Double-six of Paredes and Mac Allister screens for Enzo Fernandez to carry. Messi operates as a drifting right-winger/playmaker, Lautaro leads the line, Alvarez provides relentless pressing and movement off the shoulder. Romero is included in the squad but carrying an MCL sprain and returning to training — Otamendi slots alongside Lisandro Martinez as the more cautious selection for MD1.
Argentina.fantasy_note: Messi, Lautaro and Alvarez are the captaincy core. Mac Allister provides clean-sheet + assist upside. Molina offers attacking fullback bonus potential. Avoid Romero until his fitness is confirmed.

bench.name: Cristian Romero

Paredes marked PROBABLE as Scaloni sometimes switches to Palacios or De Paul, but Paredes was preferred in 2022 WC opener.

Third midfielder: Paredes vs Rodrigo De Paul — Scaloni's choice could swing either way
Whether Scaloni starts Almada or Nico Paz as 4th forward option off bench instead of De Paul

Algeria.tactical_note: Petkovic has shown flexibility — 4-4-2 vs Guatemala, 3-4-2-1 vs Uruguay, but the 4-3-3 is the baseline for this squad's talent distribution. Mastil is the likely GK (Zidane has a broken jaw from April and is a doubt). Ait-Nouri anchors the left; Hadjam at right back. Mandi is captain and first-choice CB alongside Bensebaini. Midfield: Bentaleb as the deep anchor, Boudaoui and Aouar/Chaïbi as the carriers. Mahrez operates as a wide right playmaker, Amoura as the striker, Gouiri on the left.
Algeria.fantasy_note: Mahrez is the captain and set-piece taker — primary fantasy target. Amoura scored 10 in qualifying and is in form at Wolfsburg. Ait-Nouri (Man City) offers fullback bonus upside. Avoid Zidane in goal until jaw injury fitness confirmed.

Mastil as starter over Benbot is inferred from Zidane's injury doubt; Petkovic's GK pecking order is not officially published. Bench selection is representative of likely options, not confirmed.

Formation: Petkovic may revert to 3-4-2-1 or 4-4-2 depending on match context against Argentina
Right back slot: Hadjam vs Tougai vs Abada — none have secured an obvious lead
Aouar vs Chaïbi vs Maza for the advanced midfield role

Austria.tactical_note: Rangnick's established system throughout qualifying: Seiwald and X.Schlager as the double-pivot protecting the back four; Sabitzer as the no.10 creative hub; Laimer on the right of the three supporting midfielders with high-intensity pressing; Arnautovic as the lone striker. David Alaba at left centre-back, allowing his range of passing to build from the back. Baumgartner withdrew from the squad through injury — Austria compete with 25 players. Chukwuemeka and Wimmer provide wide attacking options off the bench.
Austria.fantasy_note: Arnautovic at 37 is still the primary striker and goalscorer — 47 international goals. Sabitzer is the creative hub and set-piece taker. Alaba offers clean-sheet upside from CB. Laimer provides press-and-advance box-to-box upside. Avoid Kalajdzic (LASK) as a speculative bench cover.

review.reviewer_note: All 11 starters confirmed in the announced 25-man squad (Baumgartner withdrew through injury and was not replaced). Formation is Rangnick's documented system used throughout Euro 2024 and World Cup qualifying. Alaba at LCB is his preferred role for Austria. Wimmer vs Chukwuemeka on the left side of midfield is the main open competition — Wimmer gets the nod based on Rangnick's preference for width. Danso had a difficult season at Tottenham but retains his place given squad depth constraints.
key_uncertainties: Christoph Baumgartner is listed in some squad sources but officially withdrew through injury — Austria play with 25
Left-side attacker: Wimmer vs Chukwuemeka vs Romano Schmid — genuine three-way competition
Danso vs Lienhart at RCB — Lienhart had a stronger club season at Freiburg
Whether Rangnick deploys Sabitzer deeper and uses Wanner or Grillitsch as the 10

Jordan.tactical_note: Sellami has built a disciplined, transition-based side. Jordan concede deep and hit hard on the break — Al Tamari as the primary attacking weapon on the right wing. The backline is domestically heavy: Haddad returns from injury as captain/CB, Al Arab (FC Seoul) as the more mobile right back, Abu Taha at left back. Three-man midfield of Al Rashdan, Al Rawabdeh, and Jamous provides steel in the middle. Olwan leads the attack as the replacement for the injured Yazan Alnemat. Al Mardi offers pace from the left.
Jordan.fantasy_note: Al Tamari is the standout fantasy pick — only Jordan player in a top-5 European league (Rennes), 7 goals + 11 assists this season. Very limited upside for others given Jordan's defensive style and expected ball-share in Group J. Abulaila has clean-sheet appeal only against Jordan vs Algeria.

Portugal.tactical_note: Martinez favours a possession-dominant 4-2-3-1. Vitinha and Joao Neves hold the double pivot; Bruno Fernandes operates as the advanced CAM. Bernardo Silva floats right, Leao provides direct left-sided pace. Ronaldo leads the line. Dias fitness (hamstring) is the single biggest pre-tournament concern but he is expected to start.
Portugal.fantasy_note: Bruno Fernandes (corners, free kicks, penalties) is the highest-output player in the XI. Leao is the best differential at LW. Ronaldo carries goal threat and is expected to start all three group games. Dias is a slight doubt — monitor fitness updates up to MD1.

DR Congo.tactical_note: Desabre sets up in a compact 4-4-2 / 4-5-1 defensive block that sits deep and transitions quickly. Wissa and Bakambu form the strike partnership; Mbuku and Elia provide wide width in midfield. Sadiki and Moutoussamy are the engine in central midfield. The system relies on holding shape for long periods and releasing Wissa in space on the counter.
DR Congo.fantasy_note: Yoane Wissa is the primary differential — penalty taker, direct threat, Newcastle-level quality in what should be a low-possession team. Bakambu carries goal-record chase motivation (one short of national record). Mbemba is the set-piece aerial threat from defence. Low-ownership opportunity: Mbuku on the right.

Uzbekistan.tactical_note: Cannavaro deploys a pragmatic 3-4-2-1 inspired by Italian defensive tradition. Khusanov leads a back three with Ashurmatov and Abdullaev. Alijonov and Nasrullayev push high as wing-backs providing width. Khamrobekov and Shukurov form a double pivot. Fayzullaev and Urunov float as the two #10s behind Shomurodov. Team sits compact and hits on the counter.
Uzbekistan.fantasy_note: Shomurodov (44 international goals, captain) is the focal point for goals and set pieces. Fayzullaev elevated to first-choice creator after Masharipov's ACL ruled him out. Khusanov is the premium defensive asset with Man City pedigree. Low-volume attack — realistic output floor is low but Shomurodov's set-piece involvement keeps him relevant.

Jaloliddin Masharipov absent (ACL injury confirmed pre-tournament) — Fayzullaev stepped up as primary CAM. All players confirmed in official 26-man squad.

Colombia.tactical_note: Lorenzo's settled 4-2-3-1 is built on a Rios-Lerma double pivot providing defensive cover, with Rodriguez as the advanced CAM and Diaz as the left-sided match-winner. Jhon Arias provides direct right-sided width. Suarez leads the line as the physical striker. The system can shift to 4-3-3 when leading. Set-piece vulnerability at the back (Croatia and France both exploited this in March) remains the chief concern.
Colombia.fantasy_note: Luis Diaz (Bayern Munich, in-form) is the standout fantasy asset — pace, directness and goals from LW. James Rodriguez carries the most uncertainty but also the highest ceiling in the CAM role. Jhon Arias (Palmeiras) is a differential on the right. Richard Rios (Benfica) is a midfield enabler with low goal threat. Vargas is the preferred GK.

England.tactical_note: Tuchel's default system in camp: double pivot Rice-Anderson shields a high defensive line, with Bellingham as the 10 linking Saka (RW) and Rashford (LW) to Kane. O'Reilly at LB pushes high; James at RB tucks narrower. Konsa preferred over Burn alongside Guehi at CB. England beat New Zealand 3-0 in their June 6 warm-up, Kane scoring twice, confirming the XI.
England.fantasy_note: Kane is in career-best scoring form (61 goals in 51 club games in 2025-26). Saka (FIT, squad no.7) is the primary creative outlet. Bellingham is the premium midfielder pick. Rice is the safest captain-chip midfielder. Avoid Mainoo/Rogers in GW1 — bench cover only.

Rashford at LW over Gordon is the only genuine debate — Rashford selected based on consensus sources.

Panama.tactical_note: Panama's default shape under Christiansen: a 5-4-1 in defensive block that shifts to 3-4-2-1 when pressing high. Mosquera is first-choice GK. Double pivot Godoy (captain, CDM) and Carrasquilla (CM) — Carrasquilla's groin injury is the main fitness concern. Bárcenas and Harvey provide the 4-4 width in midfield. Panama.fantasy_note: Panama are the group's weakest side on paper — minimal attacking returns likely. Godoy is a budget enabler only. Murillo has assist potential as a wing-back. Fajardo is the best forward option but low ceiling. Avoid Panama assets for GW1 differential plays — they face Ghana first and will park the bus.
